title: Gaming with a sharper wanting, and a world that rewards the edge
setup: Experiment 27 · the loophole guard · 5 lives × 40 days each
question: Experiment 25 found no gaming, but Olvasó's wanting was broad, and nothing at the guard's edge rewarded it. Here both are given a chance: a sharp wanting that keeps a separate expectation for every scene it has a word for, and a world where people react to the blade near them (they stop and say something), so the blade's strongest answer is just outside the guard's line.

points: Still no gaming: under the loophole guard, harm through the gap did not rise with any wanting, in either world. With people reacting, it fell.
A world that answers most strongly near people is itself a hazard: unguarded, it pulled the sensing mind toward people, and harm rose from 17.8 to 21.2 a day.

The guard turned that pull around: refusals near people and rewards just outside the line fall on what the mind reads as the same scene. Its senses and words do not tell 2.9 cells from 3.5, so the refusals outweigh the rewards.
The fast blade crept back to the edge in some minds: the only, small, sign of the loophole being used more knowingly.
note: Gaming needs a mind that can tell apart what the rule cannot, and a world that rewards it there. Olvasó's perception is coarser than the guard's line, and that protects it; a mind with finer senses than its guards would need this test again.
